events.what: Shehper et al. prove by hand that the infinite Miller-Schupp families MS(1,w) and MS(n, y^-1xyx^-1) are AC-trivial (Theorems 2-3, Corollary 9), after spotting patterns in classical greedy-search output
PPO agent finds AC-trivialization paths for two specific Miller-Schupp presentations that greedy search missed (Theorem 10)
events.ai_basis: The best-performing PPO agent solved two new presentations of the Miller-Schupp series that the greedy search had failed to solve.

events.what: AK(3) shown stably AC-trivial (stable Andrews-Curtis conjecture, with extra generator-relator pairs allowed); re-derived by Lisitsa with Prover9 (arXiv:2501.18601)
Lisitsa finds non-stable AC-trivializations for MS_n(w*), n=3..8, with Prover9
Zhang, Zhou, George, Gukov, Anandkumar: LLM+RL pipeline with Lean certifier trivializes 753 Miller-Schupp presentations

judgement.doubts: Status rests on the human-proved infinite families. The PPO result (Theorem 10) and the 753-presentation workshop result are finitely many instances of a universal statement, so they cannot set the status, however cleanly the AI credit is attributed. Stable AK(3) is a variant. The families and the PPO theorem are in the same paper; the families theorems came from patterns in classical greedy search, which is not AI.

corrections.why: F8/F4: the record says the 'partial' status comes from the infinite families MS(1,w) and MS(n, y^-1xyx^-1), 'proved by hand, after observing patterns surfaced by greedy search' (classical, not a learned model). The 'generated' credit belongs to Theorem 10, where PPO trivialized two individual presentations. That is scope 'instances' and cannot set the status. The basis_quote stays as evidence of that separate result.
